title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' Grothendieck studies the genus-1 analogue of the Galois/Teichmüller action. A profinite group M, an extension built from the profinite completion of 𝔊 = GL(2,ℤ) and Galois data, maps to GL(2,Ẑ) via Θ_M. ρ is the j = 0 point, the one with automorphism group of order 6. L_ρ is the stabiliser of ρ in SL(2,ℤ), cyclic of order 6. D_ρ is its normaliser in GL(2,ℤ), dihedral of order 12. Π_0 is a torsion-free normal subgroup of 𝔊 of index 24; the next page factors 𝔊/Π_0 through GL(2,ℤ/4). Z_ρ and N_ρ are a centraliser-like and a normaliser-like subgroup of M attached to ρ, and N_ρ* is a variant of N_ρ. μ = μ_2 (or a group of roots of unity) is a direct factor.

On the previous page Grothendieck examined four subgroups of Z_ρ (labelled (39)). Using the characters ε_2, ε_3 and the element τ' = τσ, he showed that only M'(-j) = Z^!_{ρ0} fails to be normal in N_ρ.

This page continues:
(i) The other subgroups, after (semi-)direct product with μ_2, give normal subgroups of N_ρ.
(ii) The smallest of them is M^0(-j), of index 24 in N_ρ*. So N_ρ*/M^0(-j) has order 24.
(iii) D_ρ sits inside N_ρ* and maps to this quotient by (44): D_ρ → N_ρ*/M^0(-j).
(iv) Injectivity: the kernel lies in L_ρ = D_ρ ∩ Z_ρ. More precisely it lies in L_ρ ∩ Z^!_{ρ0} ⊂ L_ρ ∩ M_0^! = L_ρ ∩ Π_0 = {1}, because the finite group L_ρ meets the torsion-free Π_0 trivially.
(v) Hence D_ρ (order 12) has index 2 in N_ρ*/M^0(-j), just as D_ρ has index 2 in 𝔊/Π_0. Indeed D_ρ ∩ Π_0 = 1 and |𝔊/Π_0| = 24.
(vi) This motivates the conjectural isomorphism N_ρ*/M^0(-j) ≅ 𝔊/Π_0, compatible with the embeddings of D_ρ. It is proved on the next page as Proposition (46), via M → GL(2,Ẑ) → GL(2,ℤ/4) → 𝔊/Π_0.

Purpose: describe the normaliser in the arithmetic/profinite group M of the 'tangential' structure at the special point j = 0, and identify its finite quotient with the discrete group 𝔊/Π_0. This is part of computing the local data at the special points (orbifold points) of the modular curve M_{1,1} for the genus-1 lacet equations.
errors: (44) is written with M^0(J); the sign is dropped, and the intended group is M^0(-J) as elsewhere on the page.
The interlinear annotation '24 = μ_2·L_ρ' is numerically inconsistent: |μ_2|·|L_ρ| = 12. It presumably means a group of the shape μ_2 × (something of order 12, e.g. D_ρ), or it is a hasty note.

Order bookkeeping: the kernel of (44) is directly L_ρ ∩ M^0(-j). The chain through Z^!_{ρ0} and M_0^! is valid only if M^0(-j) ⊂ Z^!_{ρ0} ⊂ M_0^!, which the previous page does indicate. No substantive error.

ideas.what: Normal subgroups of the normaliser N_ρ of the j=0 point data, obtained from subgroups of Z_ρ by product with μ_2. The smallest, M^0(-j), has index 24 in N_ρ*.
ideas.modern_name: decomposition/inertia structure at the orbifold (elliptic) point j=0 of M_{1,1} under a profinite Teichmüller–Galois group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura, Ihara–Matsumoto, Hatsui–Nakamura and others (Galois action on π1 of once-punctured elliptic curves and on M_{1,1})

ideas.what: Injectivity of the finite dihedral group D_ρ (order 12) into the order-24 quotient, using torsion-freeness of Π_0.
ideas.modern_name: finite subgroups meet torsion-free normal subgroups trivially

ideas.what: Anticipated identification N_ρ*/M^0(-j) ≅ 𝔊/Π_0 (GL(2,ℤ) modulo a torsion-free index-24 subgroup), compatible with D_ρ; proved on the next page via reduction to GL(2,ℤ/4).
ideas.modern_name: comparison of local profinite normaliser with finite congruence quotient of GL(2,ℤ)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine group-theoretic bookkeeping step (index count plus an injectivity argument via torsion-freeness) inside a longer unpublished computation of local data at j=0 for genus-1 Teichmüller/Galois actions. It is technically part of unpublished material, but it carries no new idea beyond what the surrounding computation already does.
transcription_corrections: First word is likely 'maintenant' (continuing 'Les autres donnent maintenant, par produit … direct avec μ_±'), not 'maximum'. The '1/2' may be 'semi-' or a stray mark.
(44) should read D_ρ ↪ N_ρ*/M^0(-J), with the minus sign as elsewhere.
Around 'normalisateur de L_ρ dans Gl(2,ℤ)' the text reads roughly '…, groupe isomorphe à D_6, et d'ordre 12'. The '[?]' passage refers to D_6, the dihedral group of order 12.
The 'puisque' line is L_ρ ∩ Z^!_{ρ0} ⊂ L_ρ ∩ M_0^! = L_ρ ∩ Π_0 = {1}, with 'puisque' preceded by struck text.
